comments.text: Sets up the title video and interrupts, initializes the music, checks the high score and runs the title loop before dispatching driving file one.
Shows the message rows and the high-score sequence, requests a music fade and waits at the press-fire prompt before dispatching the loader.
High byte of the synthetic return address pushed before the loader transfer. The no-opening option substitutes $68.
Low byte of the synthetic return address. The loader’s return advances to the next address.
File index passed to the loader. The wrapper changes the default $0D opening to drive file $01 when the option requests it.
Nine loaded zero bytes between the title’s jump into the loader and the start of the bitmap display routine.
Selects VIC bank $4000 and $D018=$78 for the title bitmap. Copies four pages from $5800 to colour RAM and selects multicolour bitmap mode.
High byte of the title colour plane source. Increments as the four pages are copied from $5800.
High operand of the copy to colour RAM, incremented with each completed page before the bitmap mode is selected.
Page copier for the picture planes. Uses Y to walk each page and increments the source and destination page operands before the next page.
High byte of the page copier’s source address. Advances after each 256-byte block.
Byte patched when the page copier steps to its next destination page. The current page destination operand is based at $6000.
Masks CIA interrupts, clears SID volume, disables VIC IRQs and acknowledges latched VIC flags.
Installs the press-fire sprite pointer rows, waits for fire and clears the sprite-enable register.
Four rows of eight VIC sprite pointers, followed by four horizontal offsets. $08E5 copies all 36 bytes to $0DAB for the press-fire prompt.
Redirects the title IRQ to the four sprite-row handler and sets all slot colours for messages.
Installs the title message IRQ, clears colour RAM and sets the first message record and row indices.
Low operand patched when the message loop advances by 36 bytes to the next record.
Page byte of the message-row source. It is advanced with carry when the source walks to the next 36-byte record.
Eight stored values between the title message loop and the first 36-byte message record.
Title message record 1. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 2. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 3. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 4. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 5. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 6. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 7. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 8. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 9. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
Title message record 10. Thirty-two sprite pointers for the four eight-sprite rows, followed by four horizontal offsets. The loop at $0947 copies them to $0DAB.
The message reader at $0947 tests for $FF to return after the last record. The following entry begins the timed wait helper.
Sets Y to zero before the title wait. Repeated decrements wrap through the full byte range unless fire ends the wait early.
Polls the active-low fire bit and waits for the title’s raster tick. A new fire press ends the wait before its countdown expires.
Prevents the same held fire press from ending successive waits.
Uses a fresh-control latch and matches eight active-low CIA joystick bits. Completing the sequence sets the byte at $0402 and increments the border colour.
Eight CIA joystick masks checked by $0B30. The sequence tests up twice, right twice, down twice and left twice.
Next position in the eight-input title sequence. A mismatch resets it.
Suppresses repeat readings until the joystick port returns to neutral.
Selects the score raster handler, programs the common eight X positions and two high X bits and fills colour RAM with colour ten.
Holds each five-byte record for the configured row interval, advancing to the next until the byte offset reaches $2D.
Scans the packed score table in five-byte steps and shifts lower entries before opening the initials editor. A VICE store watch confirmed the five writes to the top record with a test score of 9999.
Low operand of the absolute decrement of the score-row timer at $0BFF. The editor advances through the rows before accepting the three initials.
Waits for the active raster tick at $0E83 to change before returning.
Clears the $D400–$D7FF I/O addresses, zeros the zero-page working bytes above the CPU port and configures CIA1 for reading the joystick.
Selects VIC bank $C000 and $D018=$34, turns on multicolour sprites, sets the shared colours and initializes the screen’s sprite pointers.
Copies the incoming colour in A across four pages beginning at $D800.
High byte of the current fill destination, incremented after each 256-byte page.
Eight low X positions for the score sprites. The high bits for the rightmost two are written separately to $D010.
Writes title IRQ $0D3C and NMI $0E70 into RAM hardware vectors, selects the first title raster handler and enables the VIC raster interrupt.
Saves A, X and Y in the restore operands, clears decimal mode, acknowledges the VIC raster interrupt and dispatches the title’s changing raster target.
Low byte of the current raster subroutine destination, patched by the title phase or IRQ.
High byte of the current raster subroutine pointer.
Sets a common sprite Y, writes X coordinates spaced twenty-four pixels apart, and copies eight pointers to $CFF8 from the table indexed by the title’s four raster rows.
Low operand of the raster handler’s music tick. The region wrapper can redirect the call to the divider.
Patched high byte of the message-row music update call. The following instructions set the next raster line.
Runtime configuration for the four sprite rows. The raster sorts out eight pointers at a time and $0D68 reads the four per-row horizontal offsets at $0DCB.
Advances the title tick, starts the next score row, ticks the music and maps three initial letters plus four BCD digit nibbles from the five-byte records at $0405 into sprite pointers.
Low operand of the JSR from the high-score raster to the music tick. Patched at $0F0F for the alternate divider.
The region option can patch this upper byte of the JSR at $0DE8. The raster then positions the score sprites and loads their pointers from the selected five-byte score record.
Loads the final packed score digit as a sprite pointer, then clears the last pointer and colours the selected edit row.
Saved X patched into the IRQ return sequence.
Saved Y operand loaded at the IRQ epilogue.
Saved accumulator restored before the raster returns.
Single RTI used as the title’s NMI entry.
Resets the raster line to zero and restores the high-score handler pointer for the next frame.
Incremented by the first high-score row and at the end of the four-row title message raster. Timed waits compare successive reads.
Starting five-byte record offset used by the high-score raster.
Counts down between changes to the first visible score entry while the title scrolls them.
Y for the current score row, advanced by forty between rows.
Five-byte record offset of the row being edited. The raster draws that row with a distinct colour.
Raster publishes the selected record’s Y so the initials editor can wait for it to reach the target row.
The editor only tests the left and right buttons every eighth title tick.
The initials editor uses this latch to advance to the next letter once per fresh fire press. Release clears it.
Loaded zeros after the high-score editor’s last working byte and up to the region option wrapper at $0F00.
Applies the release’s two title options by patching the alternate music-tick target or title timing instructions, then jumps to $0812.
When the immediate counter is nonzero decrements it and jumps to the music tick. When zero, reloads six and returns without ticking.
Holds the current countdown when the title’s region option changes the raster JSR targets to $0F34.
Enters the drive wrapper at $0646 with X=2, A=$9A, Y=1 after an eligible score entry. The option at $02B3 bypasses this route.
Four pages of per-cell colour bytes. $0889 copies this source to $D800 before the title switches to the sprite logo phase.
Packed colour pairs for the 40-by-25 screen cells in the title bitmap phase. VIC bank $4000 and $D018=$78 address this plane.
Title bitmap cell rows 1 through 3. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 4 through 6. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 7 through 9. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 10 through 12. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 13 through 15. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 16 through 18. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 19 through 21. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 22 through 24. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
Title bitmap cell rows 25 through 25. Each character row has 320 bytes in pairs-of-pixels multicolour format.
The title bitmap allocation ends at $7FFF. These 192 zero bytes follow the last visible cell row. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $7F40–$7FFF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $8000–$83FF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $8400–$87FF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $8800–$8BFF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $8C00–$8FFF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $9000–$93FF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $9400–$97FF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $9800–$9BFF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $9C00–$9FFF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $A000–$A3FF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $A400–$A7FF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $A800–$ABFF.
Zero fill in the title asset block between the bitmap bank and the fixed $B000 music entry. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $AC00–$AFFF.
Jumps to $B131 to clear the title player state and initialize SID.
Jumps to the music update at $B16C, called by the raster handler.
Embedded PETSCII text identifies The Fast Lane as Sean Connolly’s title tune and credits him for the music and effects players.
Per-voice divider decremented at $B1E0 before note duration advances. Reloads from $B09E.
Reload value for each voice’s tick divider. The order stream’s $F0-range command replaces it.
A nonzero flag makes the driver write zero to the voice’s SID control register, clearing the gate and waveform bits, then return.
Length of the current kind of pattern note. A pattern command at least $80 loads the duration before the following event.
Remaining note or hold duration in music ticks. Expiry enters the pattern command reader.
Byte index of the next event in the current note pattern for each voice.
Index into the voice’s sequence of patterns and order commands.
Number of further plays before the voice advances to the next pattern in its order stream.
Transposed note number used as the base for pitch-sequence offsets.
Current output pitch after interpreting the instrument pitch row. Used as the index into the SID frequency tables.
Low byte of the target frequency value during portamento and after a change in the pitch row.
High byte of the target frequency, also used to compare and end a pitch slide.
Low byte of the current pitch word. The voice adjusts it while writing portamento or pitch movement.
Three high-frequency bytes for the current pitches, paired with $B0BF. Two further three-byte lanes appear before the instrument index at $B0CB.
Three selected instrument numbers, used for eight-byte records beginning at $B74D. Two further three-byte lanes precede the pulse accumulator.
Low byte accumulator for each voice’s pulse width. The pulse update writes it to SID pulse register low.
Integer pulse width per channel. The upward sweep adds the fractional carry and the downward sweep subtracts the fractional borrow before checking the respective bound.
Low-byte pulse width delta taken from an instrument record.
Selects add or subtract in the pulse width update. Toggles when the high byte reaches its current limit.
Lower pulse width bound loaded from the high nibble of the instrument’s packed limit byte.
Upper pulse width bound loaded from the low nibble of the packed limit byte.
Pitch sequence index from the instrument record. The reader scales it by ten and adds the current row offset.
Index of the instrument’s waveform sequence. The reader multiplies by ten to get the row base.
Pattern number selected by the current voice order entry. Used to look up the pattern address.
The five-bit voice transposition command. Added to pattern note values before frequency lookup.
Low frequency step applied by the late-note modulation routine. Reloaded for a fresh instrument.
Per-wrap increment to the modulation step. Taken from the instrument record.
Upper byte of the late-note frequency step, modified by carry and used in frequency addition and subtraction.
Counter for the later pitch oscillation. The routine changes its direction at phase boundaries and restarts it at eight.
Nonzero makes the tick update the pitch slide toward the target frequency. Cleared on reaching the target high byte.
Pattern-supplied slide rate. Multiplies by four to get the word added or subtracted on each tick.
Low part of the running frequency during a slide, initialized from its starting note.
High part of the running slide frequency. Compared against the target high byte.
Low byte of the slide rate multiplied by four, used in the slide’s frequency arithmetic.
High byte of the slide rate times four, added or subtracted alongside the low step.
Pitch-sequence enable flag. A $FE byte in the row clears it until a new note.
Mask applied before sending waveform bits to the SID. A gate-off pattern event clears bit zero.
Low byte of each of the three order-stream addresses. Paired with $B119.
High byte of each of the three channel order addresses. $B45F copies this lane to $F9.
Next byte in the instrument’s pitch sequence. Resets on note attack or through a loop command.
Index of the next SID waveform byte within its instrument sequence row.
Selected logical voice for the shared filter control.
Current cutoff compared to the target before the next SID write.
Target cutoff high byte that the current value approaches.
Increment or decrement for each filter tick.
Target loaded after the cutoff reaches the current one.
Preserves the high nibble of the SID master control through a volume fade step.
Scaled instrument offset recorded when changing the filter parameters.
Saved pattern cursor during note frequency lookup.
Counts to twenty before one unit of master volume is removed.
Flag checked before starting the title music volume countdown.
Last stored filter mode and master volume for SID register $D418.
Envelope attack and decay selected from the current instrument.
Envelope sustain and release selected from the current instrument.
Saved X voice index while the update uses indexed frequency tables.
Saved Y starting offset into the SID registers for the selected voice.
Initializes three voice-lane counters and flags, clears SID registers and starts the volume at fifteen with low-pass filtering.
Moves the SID cutoff toward the target, handles the volume fade and dispatches the three voice lanes to $B1D5.
Saves X as the logical voice and Y as the SID register lane. Advances the duration, fetches a new event on expiry and applies wave and pitch sequences on continuing notes.
Reads the channel order stream via $F8/$F9 and resolves a pattern through $B88D/$B8AC. Then reads duration, instrument, filter and pitch events via $FA/$FB.
Stored bytes of LDA ($FA),Y before the filter command test. The preceding branch dispatches directly to its comparison.
Converts pattern event bytes from $70 through $7D into the filter route register value and records the channel that supplies filter parameters.
Stored LDA ($FA),Y preceding the pitch path reached from the branch at $B54C.
Transposes the note, advances the pattern and order cursors on the terminal marker and reloads the instrument. Writes the ADSR, pulse width, frequency and control to the voice registers.
Advances the pattern after a hold or gate-off event. Applies repeat and order-loop handling and resumes the active voice without reinitializing its envelope.
Low bytes of the 96 SID frequency words that translate the transposed note numbers.
High bytes paired with $B68D. The voice update uses them to write the high SID frequency register.
Fourteen eight-byte instrument records. The voice handler scales the instrument number by eight and reads waveform and pitch sequences, the ADSR envelope and pulse and filter settings.
Byte one of each instrument record, selecting a ten-byte pitch sequence.
Byte two of the instrument record, written to the SID attack and decay register for a new note.
Byte three of the instrument record, written to the SID sustain and release register.
Upper nibble starts a pitch step. The lower nibble sets its increment during the modulation sequence.
Packed pulse-width step and initial high pulse value in two nibbles.
High nibble selects the alternate filter cutoff and the low nibble selects the filter step.
Pitch sequence selector in the eight-byte instrument record. The driver copies it to the current voice state.
Ten ten-byte rows for waveform and gate bits. The tick at $B253 advances the selected row and $FF names a row offset to loop to.
The second byte may be read as a destination when the first value is the $FF waveform-loop marker. It is part of the same packed waveform rows.
Eight ten-byte rows for pitch changes. The tick at $B28D adds relative offsets to the note, loads absolute pitches above its comparison threshold, loops with $FF and stops a row on $FE.
The second byte may be read as a pitch-sequence loop destination on $FF. Other bytes follow the same ten-byte pitch row layout.
The voice reader at $B1FC takes the high nibble for the per-tick pulse update. The note attack at $B5BE uses the low nibble as the upper bound.
Initial SID control bytes indexed by instrument for note attack. $B5C6 reads the byte and clears then sets the gate bit.
Low bytes of 31 music pattern addresses. The player combines them with the high bytes at $B8AC and reads the chosen pattern through $FA/$FB.
Pattern pointer high bytes paired with $B88D. $B4C2 reads this lane for the pattern index selected by the voice order.
Order list for SID voice 1. $B467 reads pattern numbers and tempo, transpose or repeat commands. The final $FF and offset $00 loop the order stream.
Order list for SID voice 2. $B467 reads pattern numbers and tempo, transpose or repeat commands. The final $FF and offset $00 loop the order stream.
Order list for SID voice 3. $B467 reads pattern numbers and tempo, transpose or repeat commands. The final $FF and offset $00 loop the order stream.

Loader-written zero span after the final title tune pattern’s terminal $FF at $BE57 and before the title font at $C000.
Title font sprite slots $00–$0F. All carry 21 rows of three pixel bytes per row. The low ten indices are used directly by the high-score digit display.
Title font sprite slots $10–$1F. The title message at $08FB and the rows from $098F include pointers into this portion of the font.
Seven remaining title font slots $20–$26. The message loop writes pointer $26 across the display to blank the rows.
Nine zero-filled 64-byte slots after the last title font sprite. The following page at $CC00 is the screen selected by $D018=$34.
Forty columns by twenty-five rows of loaded character codes. The title selects this screen and the character set at $D000 with $D018=$34 in VIC bank $C000.
Sixteen zero bytes between the last screen cell and the eight sprite-pointer bytes.
Eight bytes loaded as zero and overwritten by the title raster. They select the font sprite in each physical VIC slot.
Low half of the title character image selected by $D018=$34 in VIC bank $C000.
Upper half of the title character image read by the VIC at the same time that CPU accesses here address SID mirrors.
